mainTopic: Permitted growths cancelling a forbidden original plant, the close of פרק הנודר מן הירק, and the new משנה on vows limited by time, with רבי ירמיה's rule that a 'today' vow needs release from a חכם
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of whether permitted growths can cancel out a forbidden original plant of תרומה. It is challenged from a משנה that says growths of תרומה are still תרומה, and from a משנה about טבל. It answers by narrowing the case: we mean growths of growths, even in plants like onions whose seed stays whole, and specifically where those growths became bigger than the original part. Then the פרק הנודר מן הירק ends with a הדרן. A new משנה begins about a קונם vow on wine tied to time: 'today', 'this week', 'this month', 'this year', or 'this seven-year cycle' end with that calendar unit. Saying 'one day' or 'one week' instead runs a full measured period. Vows 'until פסח' depend on the exact wording, and רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about 'until before פסח'. The גמרא then quotes רבי ירמיה, who says a 'today' vow still needs release from a חכם at nightfall. רב יוסף explains that this is a rabbinic safeguard so that people do not confuse 'today' with 'one day'.

steps.title: Can permitted growths cancel out a forbidden original?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that permitted growths can cancel out forbidden תרומה, using a משנה that says growths of תרומה are themselves תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can something permitted cancel out something forbidden? But we learned in a משנה: the growths of תרומה are תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier ruling that permitted growths can make the original תרומה permitted. It quotes a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If growths of תרומה are themselves תרומה, then the new growth is also forbidden. Forbidden growth cannot cancel out a forbidden original. So how could anything here count as 'permitted' and outweigh the תרומה?

keyTerms.meaning: Something permitted
Raise up / cancel out (by outnumbering)
Something forbidden
Produce that grows from planted תרומה

phrases.english: Does the permitted cancel out the forbidden?
phrases.notes: Literally 'raise up.' The idea is that the permitted part outnumbers the forbidden part and swallows it up.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
The growths of תרומה are תרומה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the earlier ruling, from before this part of the daf, that permitted growths can make planted תרומה permitted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that permitted growths can cancel out the original forbidden תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה says growths of תרומה are themselves תרומה, so there is no permitted growth to outnumber the original.

steps.title: We mean growths of growths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ruling is about the second round of growth, not the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are speaking about growths of growths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the earlier ruling was about growths that came from the growths, not direct growths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is right that the first growth of תרומה is still תרומה. But if you plant that growth again, what comes out is a second generation, and that is permitted. Only that second generation can outnumber and cancel out the original.

keyTerms.meaning: Growths of growths: the second generation of produce
We are saying / we are talking about

phrases.english: We are speaking about growths of growths.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ruling applies to a different generation of growth than the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to say that direct growths of תרומה are permitted and can cancel out the original.
steps.terutzMaskana: Direct growths stay תרומה. Only growths of growths are permitted and can cancel out the original.

steps.title: But that is already taught in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need this ruling at all, since a משנה already says growths of growths are חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this too: growths of growths are חולין!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא raises a new problem. If the ruling is only about growths of growths, it seems to add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה already says that growths of growths are ordinary, permitted produce (חולין). So if the earlier ruling only said that, it would be repeating something we already know. The גמרא wants to know what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary produce that is not holy and is permitted

phrases.english: We already learned this too:
Growths of growths are חולין!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ruling is about growths of growths.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the ruling adds nothing, since a משנה already says growths of growths are חולין.

steps.title: New point: even plants whose seed does not decay
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that growths of growths are permitted even in plants whose original seed stays whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: even in a plant whose seed does not decay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling does add something new. Growths of growths are permitted even for plants whose seed does not decay in the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some plants, like onions, keep the original planted part whole in the ground. You might think the forbidden original stays mixed in and keeps everything forbidden. The ruling teaches that even there, growths of growths are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
A plant whose seed does not decay in the ground (like an onion)

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
Even in an item whose seed does not decay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by showing what the ruling adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point: the ruling extends the rule to a harder case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed only to repeat the משנה about growths of growths.
steps.terutzMaskana: It adds that growths of growths are permitted even when the original seed stays whole.

steps.title: A משנה about טבל says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about טבל that forbids growths of growths when the seed does not decay.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: טבל: its growths are permitted when its seed decays. But a plant whose seed does not decay: even growths of growths are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new point from step 4. A משנה about טבל says that when the seed does not decay, even growths of growths are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said growths of growths are permitted even when the seed stays whole. This משנה says the exact opposite for that same kind of plant. So how can the ruling permit it?

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been taken
A plant whose seed decays in the ground (like wheat)
Forbidden

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה: טבל:
Its growths are permitted in an item whose seed decays.
But an item whose seed does not decay:
Even growths of growths are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that growths of growths are permitted even when the seed does not decay.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about טבל says that in such plants even growths of growths are forbidden.

steps.title: When the growths become bigger than the original
steps.stepSummary: The ruling teaches that when the growths become larger than the original part, the original is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us this: if the growths grew more than the original part, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer. The ruling is about a case where the growths of growths became bigger than the original planted part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about טבל is talking about a normal case, where the original still matters and keeps things forbidden. The ruling teaches something new: once the permitted growth outweighs the original, it cancels it out, and even the original becomes permitted. This brings us back to the opening idea that permitted growth can cancel out a forbidden part.

keyTerms.meaning: Increase / the larger amount
That became more
Its original, main part (what was first planted)
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: Growths of תרומה are still תרומה. Growths of growths are חולין, even in a plant like an onion, and when they become bigger than the original, they cancel it out, and even the original becomes permitted.

phrases.english: The increase where the growths became more than its original part
Is permitted: that is what it teaches us.
phrases.notes: 'Permitted' here goes back to the original planted part. Once it is outnumbered, even it is allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and closes the discussion that began in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the ruling is about growths that became larger than the original.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to permit growths of growths in such plants in every case, against the משנה of טבל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The new point is that once the growths are bigger than the original, the original itself becomes permitted.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the פרק הנודר מן הירק
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of the פרק הנודר מן הירק.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, the פרק הנודר מן הירק.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the פרק called הנודר מן הירק. It is not part of the argument. It marks the end of the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said at the end of each פרק, showing that we hope to return to learn it again. A new פרק starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: said at the end of a פרק
The name of the פרק that is ending: 'One who vows off vegetables'

phrases.english: We will return to you, the perek 'One who vows off vegetables'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the פרק after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק הנודר מן הירק is complete.

steps.title: New משנה: how long a vow for today, this week, or this month lasts
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק's משנה rules on how long a קונם vow against wine lasts when it is limited to today, this week, or this month.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says: 'Wine is קונם for me, so I will not taste it today,' it is only forbidden until nightfall. If he says 'this week,' it is forbidden the whole week, and the coming שבת counts with the week that is ending. If he says 'this month,' it is forbidden the whole month, and ראש חודש counts with the next month.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It explains how long a vow lasts when a person ties it to a time period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Today' ends at nightfall, not after a full 24 hours. A week ends with שבת, so the coming שבת is included in the vow. A new month begins with ראש חודש, so ראש חודש is not included and he may drink wine then.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used in a vow: 'this is like a קרבן to me', making it forbidden
Until it gets dark (nightfall)
This week (here שבת means the whole week)
That passed: belongs to the week that is ending
The first day of the new month
For the coming one: belongs to the next month

steps.confusionAlert: In 'שבת זו' the word שבת means a whole week, not only the day of שבת. And 'שבת שעברה' does not mean last week's שבת. It means the coming שבת counts as part of the week that is ending, so it is included in the vow.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a vow follows how people normally speak and count time: a week ends with שבת, and a month begins with ראש חודש.

phrases.english: 'Wine is קונם for me,
so I will not taste it today':
He is forbidden only until nightfall.
'This week':
He is forbidden for the whole week,
And שבת belongs to the week that is passing.
'This month':
He is forbidden for the whole month,
And ראש חודש belongs to the coming month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow for 'today' lasts until nightfall. 'This week' includes the coming שבת. 'This month' does not include the next ראש חודש.

steps.title: A vow for 'this year' or 'this seven-year cycle'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. A vow for 'this year' lasts the whole year, and the coming ראש השנה already belongs to the next year. A vow for 'this seven-year cycle' lasts the whole cycle, and the שמיטה year counts as part of the cycle it closes.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'this year', wine is forbidden all year, and the coming ראש השנה belongs to the future year. If he said 'this seven-year cycle', it is forbidden the whole cycle, including the שמיטה year that ends it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with more vows tied to a calendar unit, this time a year and a seven-year cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like 'today' or 'this month', these vows follow the calendar, not a count of days. So the vow ends when the calendar unit ends. ראש השנה is the start of the new year, so he may drink on it. The שמיטה year is the last year of its own cycle, so it is still inside the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: This year, meaning the current calendar year
The coming ראש השנה belongs to the next year, not the current one
Here: a seven-year cycle of years, not a week of days
The seventh year, the שמיטה year

steps.confusionAlert: In this משנה, 'שָׁבוּעַ' means a seven-YEAR cycle. A week of days is called 'שַׁבָּת'. Don't read 'שבוע זה' as 'this week'.

phrases.english: 'This year' — he is forbidden the whole year,
and ראש השנה belongs to the year that is coming.
'This seven-year cycle' — he is forbidden the whole cycle,
and the seventh year belongs to the cycle that passed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of calendar-based vows from step 8 (today, this week, this month).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow on 'this year' or 'this cycle' lasts until that calendar unit ends. The next ראש השנה is already outside the vow, and the שמיטה year is inside it.

steps.title: A vow for 'one day', 'one week', and the like
steps.stepSummary: If he used the word 'one' (one day, one week, one month, one year, one cycle), the vow runs a full measured period from the moment he spoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'one day', 'one week', 'one month', 'one year', or 'one seven-year cycle', he is forbidden from that moment until the same moment at the end of that period.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from calendar vows ('this day') to counted vows ('one day').
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This day' points to the calendar day, so it ends at nightfall. 'One day' measures a length of time, so it lasts a full 24 hours from when he vowed. The same applies to every unit on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: One day: a measured length of time, not the calendar day
One week (of days)
From the time on one day to the same time on the next: a full measured period

steps.whyThisMatters: This contrast between 'today' and 'one day' is exactly what the גמרא will build on right after this, in the reason it gives for רבי ירמיה's rule.

phrases.english: But if he said 'one day',
'one week', 'one month',
'one year', 'one seven-year cycle' —
he is forbidden from day to day.
phrases.notes: He means from the exact time he vowed until that same time at the end of the full period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a contrast with steps 8–9: a counted period instead of a calendar unit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow for 'one' unit of time lasts a full measured period from the moment of the vow.

steps.title: A vow 'until פסח' versus 'until it will be פסח'
steps.stepSummary: 'Until פסח' ends when פסח arrives. 'Until it will be פסח' lasts until פסח is over.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'until פסח', wine is forbidden until פסח arrives. If he said 'until it will be פסח', it is forbidden until פסח ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers vows that end at a holiday, and shows how small wording changes shift the end point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until פסח' marks פסח as the finish line, so the vow ends as פסח begins. 'Until it will be' can mean 'as long as it is פסח', so the vow lasts through the end of the holiday.

keyTerms.meaning: Until פסח: ends when פסח begins
Until it will be (פסח): read as lasting through פסח
Until it arrives
Until it goes out, meaning until it ends

phrases.english: 'Until פסח' — he is forbidden until it arrives,
'Until it will be' — he is forbidden until it goes out.
phrases.notes: The word פסח is left out but understood: 'until it will be פסח' lasts until פסח ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from units of time to vows that end at a holiday.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Until פסח' ends when פסח arrives; 'until it will be פסח' lasts until פסח ends.

steps.title: Disagreement over 'until before פסח'
steps.stepSummary: For the wording 'until before פסח', רבי מאיר says the vow ends when פסח arrives. רבי יוסי says it lasts until פסח ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'until before פסח': רבי מאיר says it is forbidden until פסח arrives. רבי יוסי says it is forbidden until פסח ends.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a מחלוקת about one unclear wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'until before פסח' could be read either way. רבי מאיר treats it like plain 'until פסח', so it ends as the holiday arrives. רבי יוסי treats it like 'until it will be', so it lasts through the end of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Until before פסח: the disputed wording

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rules: calendar wording ('today', 'this year') ends with the calendar unit; counted wording ('one day') runs a full period; holiday wording depends on the exact phrase, and 'until before פסח' is disputed.

phrases.english: 'Until before פסח',

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אָסוּר עַד שֶׁיַּגִּיעַ,
phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: he is forbidden until it arrives,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אָסוּר עַד שֶׁיֵּצֵא.
phrases.english: רבי יוסי says: he is forbidden until it goes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד לִפְנֵי הַפֶּסַח רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, disputed wording to the two clear cases in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Until before פסח' is a מחלוקת: רבי מאיר says the vow ends when פסח arrives, and רבי יוסי says it lasts until פסח ends.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: a 'today' vow still needs a חכם at nightfall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the start of the משנה about 'today'. רבי ירמיה rules that even once night falls, the person needs to ask a חכם to release the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the משנה 'קונם, wine that I taste (today)': רבי ירמיה said that when it gets dark, he needs to ask a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It returns to the משנה's first case, a vow for 'today', and quotes רבי ירמיה's rule. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will ask for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a 'today' vow lasts only until nightfall, so you would expect him to drink freely once it gets dark. רבי ירמיה adds that he still needs a חכם to release the vow. That is surprising, and the גמרא will next explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow word that makes something forbidden like a קרבן
When it gets dark
Asking a חכם to release (undo) the vow

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not saying the 'today' vow lasts past nightfall. The משנה's rule stands; he only adds that a חכם must still be asked.

phrases.english: GEMARA
'Konam, wine that I taste,' etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה's opening case, where he vowed off wine for today.

phrases.english: רבי ירמיה said:
When it gets dark, he needs to ask a Sage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לִכְשֶׁתֶּחֱשַׁךְ צָרִיךְ שְׁאֵלָה לְחָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by going back to the 'today' case from step 8 and adding a new requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after a 'today' vow runs out at nightfall, the person must ask a חכם to release it before drinking.

steps.title: Why does a 'today' vow need release after nightfall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי ירמיה's ruling that a 'today' vow needs release from a חכם even after night falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי ירמיה said what he did. It is setting up רב יוסף's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the plain wording, a vow for 'today' should end on its own when the day ends. So it is surprising that רבי ירמיה still requires going to a חכם. The גמרא wants to know what is behind this extra requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? A standard question asking for the logic behind a ruling
Asking a Torah scholar to release a vow

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking about רבי ירמיה's ruling: why go to a חכם if the day is already over?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי ירמיה's ruling in step 13
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a vow for 'today' needs release from a חכם even after it seems to have expired at nightfall

steps.title: A safeguard so 'today' is not confused with 'one day'
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the rabbis required release for a 'today' vow so that people would not confuse it with a 'one day' vow, which lasts a full 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is a rabbinic decree. The rabbis made a rule about 'today' because of 'one day'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. The release is not needed by the strict law. It is a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow for 'one day' lasts a full 24 hours from the moment he spoke, as in step 10. If people saw a 'today' vow simply end at nightfall, they might think a 'one day' vow also ends at nightfall, and they would break it too early. To prevent this mistake, the rabbis required release from a חכם even for 'today'.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Today; a vow that ends when this day ends
One day; a vow that lasts a full 24 hours from when he spoke

steps.whatToRemember: By the strict law, a 'today' vow ends at nightfall. The rabbis still require release from a חכם so that people will not think a 'one day' vow (24 full hours) also ends at nightfall.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'today' vow is still binding by Torah law after nightfall. The release is only a rabbinic safeguard, because of the 'one day' case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the rabbis sometimes add a requirement to one case only to protect a different, similar-sounding case from mistakes.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is a decree concerning 'today'
because of 'one day'.
phrases.notes: 'One day' means a full 24 hours (step 10), so people might mix the two up if 'today' just ended at night.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The release requirement is a rabbinic decree, so that 'today' is not confused with 'one day', which lasts a full 24 hours
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 'today' vow requires release from a חכם even after nightfall, as a rabbinic safeguard because of 'one day'
